title: Supporting functionals and singular boundary geometry of two-qubit entanglement of formation
abstract: We give a criterion for the existence of a global supporting affine functional for the entanglement of formation at an entangled two-qubit state. It exists if and only if the spin-flip bilinear form is nondegenerate on the support of the state, or equivalently, if the last concurrence root associated with the support is nonzero. In this case the entanglement of formation is locally Lipschitz continuous. In the degenerate case the state has rank two or three, and its projective support is tangent to the product-state quadric. For suitable perturbations outside the support, the entanglement of formation decreases as the square root of the mixing parameter. The leading term is obtained explicitly. This square-root decrease violates the one-sided Lipschitz bound required for a global supporting affine functional.
summary: This theoretical paper provides a precise mathematical criterion for determining if the entanglement of formation ($	ext{EF}$) for a two-qubit state possesses a global supporting affine functional. The existence hinges on the nondegeneracy of the state's support with respect to the spin-flip bilinear form. Failure of this condition leads to a characteristic square-root decay of $	ext{EF}$ under perturbation, demonstrating a fundamental limitation in the measure's global differentiability.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a global supporting affine functional for the entanglement of formation ($	ext{EF}$) for an entangled two-qubit state.
main_result: A global supporting affine functional exists if and only if the spin-flip bilinear form restricted to the state's support is nondegenerate. In the degenerate case, $	ext{EF}$ decreases as the square root of the mixing parameter, violating the required bound.
method: The analysis combines mathematical criteria involving the nondegeneracy of the spin-flip bilinear form with perturbation theory applied to the $	ext{EF}$ functional along specific paths.
model_or_system: The study focuses on two-qubit quantum systems, characterized by density matrices $ho$. The mathematical tools involve the concurrence, the spin-flip bilinear form ($ eta$), and the state's support ($S$).
key_observables: Entanglement of Formation ($	ext{EF}$), Concurrence ($C$), Spin-flip bilinear form ($ eta$), and Concurrence roots ($\lambda_i$).
important_parameters: The degeneracy of $ eta|_S$ (nondegenerate vs. rank two/three), and the small perturbation parameter $t$ or $\epsilon$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the state $ho$ is entangled and relies on local Lipschitz continuity established for nondegenerate supports.

paper_structure: The paper establishes the mathematical criterion for the supporting functional's existence, analyzes the nondegenerate case where local Lipschitz continuity holds, and then investigates the degenerate case using perturbation analysis to show the failure of the global bound.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical characterization of when entanglement measures are well-behaved under small perturbations is crucial for developing robust quantum information protocols and understanding the boundaries of quantum correlations.
